questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that i would be able to speak english at the chosen location. Also I looked into reviews from students who had been there before. I valued a good review highly.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Information regarding my stay was given on mail with links to the website of the university. Here most information was present.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I E-mailed with the Erasmus coordinator from the university in Ljubljana. Replies were very fast and helpful.  Also a meeting was held in the beginning of my stay for all Erasmus students. Here we were given information and had the opportunity to ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared or private rooms. These were located at different locations in Ljubljana (primarily two main dorm areas). I could choose which dorm I would like to stay at upon arrival.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Student BONI was given to all Erasmus students. This system allowed students to eat at restaurants once a day for a reduced price (for me it was maximum 5 euros a meal) 
In my dorm, there was a shared kitchen with 5 others

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A dorm is considered a shared room and the rooms are pretty small. Also my dorm was only shared with Slovenian students. I think that some other dorm areas were more used by Erasmus students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The location was good, but the dorm was very dirty when i moved in (especially the kitchen and bathroom). I had to clean it upon arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some problems during the registration process with the learning agreement, but via email they were solved.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was done through the website of university of Ljubljana. On the website they had a guide that I followed. On the wbesite I made a profile and filled in my personal information. After this they asked me to fill in some papers such as learning agreement. They also ask you to choose which departments you want to stay at. They have the choices on their website and I think it was also sent on E-mail at the beginning of the application process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help via E-mail (They responded very fast). Also they had some help on the website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied for 5 different departments and I stayed 4 of 5 i asked for. The last one was a depardment they chose for me. Overall I was very happy with the departments of my clinical rotation

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start pretty early. Especially if you want them to help with housing. Also just follow the steps on the guide and ask on E-mail if you have any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took clinical rotations on my last year of medical school. I stayed in hospital departments and I think the level was adequate

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You are given a mentor at each department that you are supposed to follow. Some are good at explaining things in English and some are not so good. It really depends. Since everything happens in Slovene it can sometimes be a little hard to follow what is going on if your mentor is not good at explaining in English.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urology
Traumatology
Cardiovascular surgery
Haematology
Cardiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Urology, Cardiovascular surgery and cardiology. I had good mentors that were interested in teaching. Surgical departments were more interesting to me as they were easier to follow without knowing the Slovene language. Cardiology was very good as I was put in the ICU and they explained a lot and let me do some physical examinations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy your own hospital uniform if you dont bring one from home. They can be bought at the medical faculty of Ljubljana.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was cheaper then expected as they have a really good student meal system. 
Public transport was a bit cheaper than expected, especially in the weekends

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have a lot of sport opportunities at the faculty, like swimming and team sports for free. 
They don't have a student bar or social area unfortunately.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend using the free sports. Also they have good Erasmus organisation in Ljubljana that organises trips around Slovenia and the nearby countries. During the week they organise parties and other social events that are great for meeting other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking in Triglav national park and the nearby mountains. Taking trips to the sea close to Italy and Croatia. Ljubljana is a pretty small city so I tried to get out of the city every weekend to visit the nature, which is cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I found it to be not so different from Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the sport activities organised by the faculty. Also the dorms are good for meeting local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I found people to be very friendly and open. 
Outdoor culture and using the nature around the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join some of the Erasmus trips. Especially in the beginning, as they are a good was of meeting people. In the clinical rotations you are sometime the only student so it is nice to meet people in other ways.
Be patient during the clinical rotations, as there sometimes is a lot of waiting time between surgeries
Bring warm clothes as it was a bit colder and more rainy than expected. Also the location is great for hiking and outdoor trips so appropriate clothes for these activities are recommended.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attend the language course at the beginning of the stay, but I met some people who were happy to have done it. It was a good way of meeting people before the actual stay began. It also helps to give some insight into the language which can be useful at the hospital.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting new awesome people 
Traveling around Slovenia and the nearby countries with friends.
Trying to live and stay for a longer time in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
I had a mentor in Traumatology that was very bad and I had to change mentor during the stay. In the end it worked out. 
Also it was sometimes hard to understand what was going on if my mentor did not have the time or will to speak english.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
